title: Broken-Symmetry States in N≥2 Landau Levels in GaAs/AlGaAs Quantum Wells: A Brief Review
content: In high Landau levels (N≥2) of two-dimensional electron systems, the interplay between electron-electron interactions and disorder gives rise to emergent collective phases, including anisotropic stripe phases and re-entrant integer quantum Hall phases (bubble phases). These phases, first observed in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells, represent broken-symmetry charge density wave states whose detailed nature continues to be intensively explored. New models incorporating quantum fluctuations, disorder effects, and nematic order have refined our understanding of these phases. Recent experimental advances have revealed intricate behaviors such as stripe orientation transitions, nematic-to-smetic transition, and anomalous nematic states. This review synthesizes the progress in probing broken-symmetry states in N≥2 Landau levels in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells, highlighting both consensus and open challenges in the field.
